gaps.title: The timing gap
gaps.problem: Nobody knows how long cooked food stays safe.
gaps.fix: Eatsly puts a safe-window clock on every listing.

gaps.title: The matching gap
gaps.problem: NGOs cannot tell if they can reach food before it spoils.
gaps.fix: Pickup ETA is checked against the clock; impossible claims are blocked.

gaps.title: The trust gap
gaps.problem: Donors never learn where their food went.
gaps.fix: Live tracking and a proof-of-delivery receipt.

gaps.title: The awareness gap
gaps.problem: Served meals are often unbalanced, and nutrition is rarely taught.
gaps.fix: A nutrition hub and nutrient tags on every listing.

roles.name: For donors
roles.promise: Turn today's surplus into someone's plate in minutes.
benefits: Post surplus in about two minutes.
The safe-until clock is calculated before you post.
Follow your food live until it is served.

roles.name: For NGOs
roles.promise: Only see food you can reach while it is still safe.
benefits: Every claim is ETA-checked against the safe window.
Filters for veg, packaged and high-protein food.
Claim in one tap — the run is tracked for you.

roles.name: For volunteers
roles.promise: Carry a claim across the city, minute by minute.
benefits: Pickups near your area and your vehicle.
Stage buttons update everyone watching in real time.
Served plates show up on the impact page.

without: Phone calls and WhatsApp forwards, hope someone answers
Nobody is sure the food is still safe to serve
Donors never hear where their food went
NGOs burn volunteer trips on listings already claimed or cold
Good food spoils while people decide who will take it
with: Post in about two minutes from the kitchen phone
A safe-window clock is on every listing, visible to everyone
An NGO is matched by pickup ETA, not by luck
Everyone follows the same live tracking page
Delivery is signed off with a proof card and the impact counts

feels.sentence: A wedding hall sees exactly where its 120 spare plates went — with a receipt, not a rumour.
The coordinator claims with confidence because the math between ETA and the clock is done for them.
The rider gets one clear run with an address, a timer and stages — not five group chats.
The plate arrives in time, balanced on the plate builder — and nothing went to the bin for it.

principles.title: Safety first
principles.text: If the clock says no, the answer is no. Expired food never changes hands.

principles.title: Speed
principles.text: Two minutes to post, one tap to claim, a countdown that everyone shares.

principles.title: Transparency
principles.text: Live tracking and proof of delivery — every plate has a visible journey.

principles.title: Nutrition
principles.text: Food that arrives on time should still feed: every listing carries nutrient tags.

roadmap: Real-time push alerts: NGOs get a buzz the second a batch inside their ETA goes live.
Verified NGO onboarding: registration checks before any claim button lights up.
Donor impact reports: a monthly receipt of meals, kg saved, and where every plate went.

steps.title: Post
steps.subject: Image: surplus buffet trays
steps.sentence: A donor posts what is left — dish, servings, last-cooked time — and the safety clock starts automatically.

steps.title: Claim
steps.subject: Image: fresh produce at a market
steps.sentence: An NGO claims a listing only when its pickup ETA lands at least 10 minutes before the safe window ends.

steps.title: Track
steps.subject: Image: volunteer on a scooter
steps.sentence: A volunteer picks up the food; everyone watching can follow every stage on a live tracking page.

steps.title: Serve
steps.subject: Image: serving line at a community kitchen
steps.sentence: The receiving NGO serves the meal on time and marks the delivery — impact counts from that moment.
